title: Occupancy and Residency Certification — Closing a Profile When the Loan Ends
content:
> An Occupancy and Residency Certification profile is closed for loan termination only when the monitored Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) loan's status is paid in full, claim terminated or rescinded, or the monitored Cedarline Summit Proprietary Reverse Mortgage loan's status is paid in full or liquidated.

The loan status is read from the loan record of the loan the profile monitors — the HECM loan or the Summit loan named on the profile.

## Closing date

The closed date is the loan's terminated date, or the date of death when the profile closes because the last certifying occupant died with no deferral.

## What does not close a profile

A loan that is merely due and payable keeps its profile open, because occupancy still governs a cure and the deferral rules until the loan ends.

## Effect of closing

A closed profile receives no notices, inspections or check-ins.

## Status table

| Monitored loan | Loan status | Profile closed for loan termination? |
|---|---|---|
| HECM | paid in full | yes |
| HECM | claim terminated | yes |
| HECM | rescinded | yes |
| HECM | due and payable | no — the profile stays open |
| Summit | paid in full | yes |
| Summit | liquidated | yes |
| Summit | due and payable | no — the profile stays open |

*Hypothetical case.* A HECM loan reaches paid-in-full status with a terminated date in some month: the profile closes, and its closed date is that terminated date, not the date the closing is entered.
